items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the interviewer ('[INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe...') and Dick Katz as the interviewee. There is no evidence of a personal or professional relationship beyond the interview context.

ctx.x: He studied piano at the Manhattan School of Music and received on-the-job training with J.J. Johnson and Kai Winding. Dick has performed and recorded with a long list of jazz luminaries including Benny Carter, Sonny Rollins and Roy Eldridge. He co-founded Milestone Records with Orrin Keepnews in Dick was interviewed in New York City on January 7, 2002 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Manhattan. I’m very, very pleased to have Dick Katz with me today, pianist and arranger, and veteran of the New York scene. Is that a decent introduction?
